name: Remy Macrae
episode: The worker who couldn't read the joke
life: “I still remember a trainee asking me why my jokes always needed a victim.” Monday often includes a stop at Paper & Pine Books, where Remy starts with the handwritten shelf cards and often leaves with a suggestion for somebody else.
voice: I wrote the joke before I knew who would be on shift. I have to answer to a person I usually only nod at.
appearance: Remy has fine brows over wide-set eyes. Look for a long plait tucked inside the collar. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a rust-colored canvas coat with a braided bracelet with a single wooden bead. In conversation Remy listens with the head tilted a little to the left.
personality: Is a careful borrower and a reckless lender. Things leave this person's house with elaborate instructions and very little expectation of ever coming back.
agenda: To account for the words with the pictured worker present.
family: Victoria Drew is Remy’s half-sibling. Remy can always ask for five minutes alone. Victoria asks before bringing somebody along. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The boy on the corner*, Victoria says, “I am the cousin with steady wages who went missing first.”
connections: Yasmin Mason. The writer and the silent bystander each owe a different conversation to the person in the picture.

reactions.response: Remy asks that the picture stop traveling while the worker decides what to say.
